articleTitle: A Flexible Enhanced-Gain Quasi-Z-Source Network with Tapped-Switched-Coupled-Inductor for Renewable Energy Application
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This study proposes a novel quasi Z-source network (qZSN) utilizing coupled inductors, designed to significantly improve voltage boost and key performance characteristics for renewable applications. By employing a three-winding tapped-switched-coupled-inductor (SCL) with two arbitrary turn ratios, the proposed qZSN topology provides not only wide voltage gain capability but also enhanced freedom in circuit design. The use of this SCL architecture minimizes both input and magnetizing current ripples, allowing for significantly smaller inductive components compared to existing state-of-the-art SCL-based ZSNs. Furthermore, the topology reduces voltage stresses on both passive and active components, leading to improvements in overall system efficiency, reliability, and durability. A comparative evaluation against conventional ZSN topologies demonstrates the superior voltage gain, reduced component size, and enhanced efficiency of the proposed design. The theoretical framework and design principles are supported by experimental validation using a DC-DC laboratory prototype, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed qZSN for practical renewable energy applications.

articleTitle: Predicting Optimal Placement of Electric Vehicle Charge Stations Using Machine Learning: A Case Study in Glasgow, UK
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Given the reduced costs of establishing Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations and the need to improve their accessibility, it is essential for EV developers and governments to identify optimized locations for new stations. This study presents a predictive modeling approach using Machine Learning to determine the optimal sites for EV charging stations in Glasgow. While various machine learning methods are available for this purpose, we focus on Linear Regression due to its simplicity and high accuracy. By analyzing a comprehensive dataset of 207 AC charging stations-including factors latitude, longitude, population density, number of kinds of plugs, total number of plugs, price per kWh, traffic conditions, distance to the nearest station, Air Quality Index (AQI), and land value - we aim to provide urban planners and policymakers with actionable insights. The study evaluates the performance of the Linear Regression model in predicting the most suitable locations for charging stations. The results indicate that the proposed model achieved impressive accuracy, with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Squared Error (MSE) values of 0.89, 0.05, and 0.08, respectively. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts in urban planning for sustainable mobility by offering a data-driven methodology for EV infrastructure development.

articleTitle: A New ZVS Interleaved Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a new auxiliary circuit for interleaved flyback converters to create soft switching conditions in the element in addition the semiconductor in the converter structure prevents the voltage spike across the switches. Also, due to the use of the ripple cancellation technique, the input current has decreased. The proposed interleaved flyback converter has been completely analyzed, a 100W laboratory sample has been developed to confirm its performance, and practical results have been provided to verify the proper performance of the circuit.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Distribution Network Utilizing Dueling Deep Q Network Algorithm Under Different Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) is one of the most popular methods that power companies use to create a reliable structure for the distribution network (DN) in critical conditions. In this research, we have used DNR to minimize power losses (PL) and voltage deviation (VD). We did this using the Dueling Deep Q Network algorithm, which is an extended version of the Q-learning (QL) algorithm combined with deep learning to create a more efficient algorithm. The proposed method was implemented on an IEEE 33-bus DN under three loading types: light, nominal, and heavy loading.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of the Proposed Isolated LLC Resonant Converter with PFM Control
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This article introduces a DC-DC converter designed for various applications, including battery chargers and electric vehicles. The input stage features an EMC/EMI filter to mitigate noise. A Power Factor Correction (PFC) circuit efficiently converts 220 V AC power into 400 V DC for the DC-DC converter's input. The converter utilizes a PID controller and Pulse Frequency (PF) modulation for switching control. This modulation technique adjusts the switching frequency in response to changes in load or input voltage, ensuring output voltage stability while maintaining high system efficiency across different load conditions. Simulation results validate the proposed converter design's effectiveness, demonstrating its ability to maintain a stable output voltage under varying conditions.

articleTitle: Federated Transfer Learning for Image-Based Solar Panel Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Renewable energy, particularly solar energy, plays a vital role in achieving sustainable development. However, maintaining solar panel efficiency requires accurate fault detection and classification to ensure optimal performance. Traditional approaches rely on centralized data collection, raising concerns about data privacy and scalability. To address these challenges, this study proposes a federated transfer learning framework that leverages the pre-trained VGG-16 model for solar panel fault classification while preserving data privacy. Transfer learning facilitates effective feature extraction, enabling classification across six fault categories, including bird-drop, dusty, and snow-covered panels. Federated learning ensures decentralized training by aggregating client updates using the FedAvg algorithm, maintaining data locality and privacy. Experimental results demonstrate that the federated model achieves a test accuracy of 74% with a final loss of 0.82, comparable to a centralized model while safeguarding sensitive data. This framework provides a scalable and privacy-preserving solution for fault detection in solar panel systems.

articleTitle: Innovative Double-Sided LCC Resonant Converter Configurations for Wireless EV Chargers with Varying Coupling Coefficients
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents novel configurations of LCC resonant converters developed to enhance the efficiency of wireless charging systems for electric vehicles (EVs). The proposed configurations address the critical challenge of reduced coupling coefficients in wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. By modifying and optimizing the resonant circuit elements, the research exhibits substantial enhancements in both power transfer efficiency and operational stability under various alignment conditions, which are essential in dynamic wireless EV charging scenarios. The optimized converter configurations are designed to achieve higher efficiency with reduced energy losses, making them suitable for practical automotive applications. The effectiveness of the proposed configurations is validated through conducting simulations using MATLAB/Simulink, showing improved efficiency and reliability in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Input Single-Output Boost Inverter Topology with Dual-Control Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Dual-Input Single-Output (DISO) boost inverter topology designed to enhance efficiency and output quality. The proposed topology utilizes a reduced component count and lower device voltage stress, leading to potential cost reductions. An LCL filter at the output stage effectively mitigates Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) to below 2.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, which complies with IEEE standards. Furthermore, the inverter employs an innovative control strategy that utilizes both the modulation index and a phase shift parameter to regulate the output voltage. This dual-control mechanism provides enhanced flexibility and precise voltage regulation under varying operating conditions and input voltage imbalances. The proposed inverter has an output power of 5 kW, and if the power is increased to 10 kW, it will enable soft switching. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DISO inverter in supplying both resistive and resistive-inductive loads with low THD under various scenarios.

articleTitle: Right-Half-Plane Zeros Free Buck-Boost DC-DC Converter with Wide Voltage Range
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This document presents a novel right-half-plane zeros (RHPZ)-free buck-boost DC-DC converter designed for a broad voltage range. It employs diode capacitor (DC) and diode inductor (DL) cells, featuring a positively regulated output voltage. The design of the proposed converter facilitates the achievement of substantial voltage gain. Furthermore, due to its dependence on a continuous input current, it is suitable for applications utilizing renewable energy sources. The fundamental operations of buck and boost modes are thoroughly analyzed, including steady-state analysis, voltage gain, and design methodology. The proposed converter is simulated in PSIM software to confirm the theoretical analyses. The results of the simulation are documented for both buck and boost modes. The input voltage operates within a range of 12V to 36V, and the output voltage is regulated to a stable 24V. The maximum output power of the converter is 100 W.

articleTitle: Ultra Step-Up DC-DC Converter Based on Voltage Multiplier Cell and Coupled Inductor
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This work introduces an innovative ultra-step-up DC-DC converter that substantially increases output voltage via a fourth-winding coupled inductor (CL) integrated with two voltage multiplier cells (VMC). The suggested converter possesses several advantages: A significant voltage amplification can be efficiently attained with a moderate duty cycle, necessitating merely one active switch. Augmenting the turn ratio of the CL diminishes the voltage stress on the active switch and diodes. The switched capacitor (SC) simultaneously captures energy from the leaky inductance, allowing for direct transfer to the output. In this paper, the steady-state analysis in continuous conduction mode (CCM) is presented to assess the voltage stress on semiconductor devices and the voltage gain. The propounded converter attains an enhanced step-up voltage gain due to its expansion. The results are utilized to evaluate the precision and efficacy of the simulation.

articleTitle: Impact of Natural Measurement Noise and Cyber Threats on Renewable Energy Metering in Smart Energy Systems: A Case Study of Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This study explores the impact of natural measurement noise and cyber threats on renewable energy metering in smart energy systems, with a focus on wind turbines. The research examines the simultaneous distribution of diverse loads supported by energy storage devices, which enhances energy resource management and system efficiency. Additionally, the influence of cyber-attacks on wind turbine power measurement devices and the effects of natural noise and measurement failures on system operating costs and performance are analyzed. The findings highlight that cyberattacks induce a mean data deviation of 17.18%, significantly disrupting system reliability, while natural noise results in a deviation of 7.4%, indicating its notable yet lesser impact. These results emphasize the importance of advanced monitoring and mitigation strategies to safeguard renewable energy systems from disruptions caused by both noise and malicious interference. The proposed framework provides actionable insights for improving the resilience and efficiency of smart energy systems in practical scenarios.

articleTitle: A Novel Z-Source Step-Up DC-DC Converter with Quadratic Boost
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Z-Source (ZS) step-up DC-DC converter for applications requiring high voltage gain. The proposed converter utilizes a unique configuration of inductors and capacitors to achieve a quadratic boost in output voltage, effectively multiplying the voltage gain compared to traditional converters. Key features include a low component count and reduced voltage stress on components, contributing to enhanced efficiency and compact design. Theoretical analysis is supported by simulation results, which confirm the converter's performance and reliability. This work significantly advances high voltage gain DC-DC converters, making them suitable for applications in renewable energy systems and other areas requiring efficient power conversion.

articleTitle: Stochastic Day-Ahead Economic Operation Scheduling of Multi-Carrier Microgrids Considering Energy Markets and Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The economic operation of multi-carrier microgrids (MGs) can harmonize the operator's objectives with those of an efficient economic system. This paper presents a day-ahead optimal scheduling model for MG operations, integrating a multi-energy market framework encompassing electricity, heating, cooling, gas, and hydrogen. It also addresses a significant research gap by incorporating demand response across all available energy carriers. Additionally, the article explores bidirectional communication between electric and hydrogen vehicle parking lots, which improves energy-balancing capabilities. To account for the system's sensitivity to uncertain parameters, the problem is formulated as a stochastic mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model. The operational performance of the MG is evaluated through four case studies, with simulation results demonstrating that the proposed strategy effectively reduces operational costs. Finally, a sensitivity analysis is conducted to validate these results.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing and Siting of Renewable Energy Sources in a ADN Using Meta-Heuristic Algorithms Considering Participation in Energy Market and Resources Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Renewable distributed generation (DG) sources have the potential to provide clean and intelligent power solutions to meet the growing energy demand. Solar and wind energy, which are prominent examples of renewable DG, offer both cost-effective and environmentally friendly energy generation. In this article to determine optimal sizing and siting of renewable energy systems (RES) in the concept of DG in an active distribution network (ADN). A new method for locating and determining the size of dgs is proposed in this study to deal with high influence of RES, which is implemented by MATLAB software. In this framework, photovoltaic panels (PV) and wind turbines (WT) have been used as DG sources, which are optimized based on the proposed algorithm, and the results before and after the involvement of DGs in the energy market are evaluated by GAMS software. Also, for accuracy in the calculations related to the overall cost of DGs, the economic parameter of CRF has also been used. The results show a 55% reduction in the cost of energy purchased from the grid and a 40.26% reduction in greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions in the scenario of with DG relative to scenario without DGs. In this regard, the amount of losses has been reduced by 14.5% relative to the scenario without DG. Furthermore, the sensitivity analysis highlighted the significant effect of DG installation on different ADN components in the optimization model.

articleTitle: Impact of Shape Variations on Thermo-Optical Response of Selected PhC Absorbers in Solar Thermophotovoltaic Converters
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) photonic crystals(Phcs) have attracted significant interest for their potential to efficiently absorb sunlight for energy harvesting. In this study, we investigate the absorption properties of three different tungsten absorbers with similar geometric features. Our results reveal that, for a given height and cross-sectional dimension, the nano-cone absorber demonstrates superior performance. We then examine the optical and thermal responses of the nano-cone absorber for use in a solar thermophotovoltaic(STPV) system. The effects of reflection and thermal radiation from both the top and bottom of the nanostructure are analyzed. Additionally, we compare the total efficiency of the nano-cones with truncated versions under varying sunlight concentration factors. The temperatures of the structures are modeled and determined based on the absorbed light. We show that concentration is a nonlinear factor that significantly influences the overall absorber efficiency.

articleTitle: Service Restoration of Distribution Networks Using Scheduling of Multiple Distributed Resources
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The service restoration problem has always been one of the most challenging issues in the operation of distribution networks. With the increasing development of distribution networks, the introduction of various technologies and tools, and the need for automation of distribution networks, solving this problem requires much more efficient and faster solutions. This paper proposes a new method to solve the SR problem. The distribution network in this study has many distributed resources including mobile power sources (MPS), distributed local generators, and repair crew (RC) that are scheduled simultaneously. Also, the service restoration problem in this paper is modeled as a MILP problem and solved by mathematical solvers. This ensures the achievement of optimal and fast solutions. The proposed method was used on a 33-bus test network and its efficiency was proven.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Single-Switch Quadratic DC-DC Converter for High-Gain Applications in Integrated Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This study introduces a DC-DC configuration with a high-voltage gain, employing a quadratic configuration specifically optimized for renewable energy applications. The recommended circuit utilizes a coupled inductor (CI) integrated with a quadratic boost structure to attain substantial voltage amplification. Its voltage gain (VG) can be adjusted by controlling two main parameters: the duty cycle of the power switches and the turn ratio of the two-winding CI, allowing for enhanced design flexibility. Key features of this converter include significant voltage gain, diminished voltage stress (VS) on switching components, a common ground (CG) shared between ports, and synchronized switch operations. A comparative analysis with similar topologies underscores the advantages of this design. The converter's efficacy is demonstrated through testing on a 360W prototype with input and output voltages of 20V and 240V, respectively.

articleTitle: Optimizing LLC Resonant Converters for Superior Efficiency Across Diverse Input Voltage and Load Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The LLC resonant converter is widely utilized in various fields for its advantageous features, including soft-switching operation, low electromagnetic interference (EMI) noise. However, its efficiency is notably reduced under light-load conditions, primarily due to the substantial difference between the switching frequency and resonant frequency, resulting in increased circulating currents and conduction losses. In this study, an innovative design procedure and control approach are proposed to mitigate the efficiency challenges associated with LLC resonant converters, particularly during light-load conditions. control Method relies on variable frequency switching and a variable capacitor. When the converter operates within the range of its two resonant frequencies, the voltage gain of the converter is manipulated through the quality factor between these frequencies. The incorporation of a variable quality factor and resonant tank enables the converter to operate precisely at its resonant frequency, resulting in a substantial enhancement in efficiency. To validate the efficacy of our proposed method, the design and control of a 48 V LLC resonant converter is implemented, capable of delivering 50 to 500 W power to feed the load. To validate the proposed approach, simulations were conducted, and the results clearly show that the converter achieves an exceptional efficiency exceeding 95% across the extensive spectrum of operating conditions, showcasing the effectiveness of our approach in overcoming the traditional efficiency limitations of LLC resonant converters.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Quadratic High-Gain DC-DC Topology with Low Voltage Stress on Semiconductors for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This research offers a high-voltage gain (VG) DC-DC structure with a quadratic configuration, specifically designed for use in renewable energy applications. The proposed topology integrates a coupled inductor (CI) with a quadratic step-up structure, achieving notable voltage enhancement. The VG of this configuration is adaptable through two primary factors: the duty cycle of the switches and the turn ratio of the two-winding CI, enabling increased flexibility in the design. Key characteristics of this converter include its high voltage gain, reduced voltage stress (VS) on elements, a shared ground between the ports, and synchronized switch operation. Comparative analysis with similar configurations highlights the advantages of this design. The converter's performance is confirmed through experimental testing on a 400W prototype, with input and output voltages of 28V and 336V, respectively.

articleTitle: Resilient Robust Polynomial-Based Frequency Control in Microgrids with RESs Using Virtual Inertia
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In modern microgrid systems, maintaining frequency stability in the presence of renewable energy sources is a significant challenge. This paper presents a resilient frequency control strategy that utilizes virtual inertia to address instability issues caused by the fluctuations in renewable energy production. The approach is based on the Robust Polynomial-Based Control Design (RPCD) method, specifically developed for microgrid applications to manage existing uncertainties. Additionally, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{H}\infty$</tex> control method is employed to assess the system's performance against disturbances and fluctuations. The study considers distributed generation from solar and wind energy and examines the system's behavior in both grid-connected and islanded modes. In the islanded mode scenario, where the microgrid is disconnected from the main grid due to issues like voltage drops or frequency mismatch, the proposed RPCD controller is evaluated for its ability to maintain microgrid stability and reliable operation. The results demonstrate that the proposed controller effectively ensures system stability under varying operational conditions.

articleTitle: A Robust Solution for Stabilizing Magnetic Characteristics of the Electromagnetics Used in EVs' On-Board Chargers
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Ferrite cores have significant applications in electronic industries, particularly as magnetic cores in transformers, filters, and other devices. However, their B-H magnetic characteristics show a strong dependency on temperature. This temperature dependency results in changes in magnetic permeability, which is critical in applications such as LLC resonant converters in electric vehicles chargers. These converters are preferred in on-board chargers due to their compact size and higher power density. However, Due to the compactness, desirable cooling faces to some limitations and the deviation of the temperature is inevitable. Such a problem changes the operating point of the converters, which may lead to loss of soft switching and stability. Therefore, it is crucial to consider and model the temperature variations in the control system, ensuring that the operating point of the converter remains stable under different working conditions. This paper proposes a new method to mitigate temperature-induced changes in the magnetic characteristics of ferrite cores. In this method, the impact of temperature is compensated using a variable inductance by a control winding in LLC resonant converters. Some simulations are conducted using ANSYS Maxwell software at temperatures <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> on an electromagnetic with an ETD29 core, to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A New ZVT Interleaved High Step-Up DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, a high step-up converter interleaved with a new auxiliary circuit has been presented so that the auxiliary circuit can be expanded to more parallel branches. On the other hand, it provides zero voltage switching conditions for the main switches and the auxiliary switch turns on under ZC and turns off under ZVZC. Therefore, the switches do not have the problem of capacitive turn-on losses. On the other hand, the auxiliary inductors are coupled with the main inductors and the energy of the auxiliary circuit is effectively transferred to the output. Due to the high gain of the converter, the voltage stress on the main switches is low. Also, because the auxiliary switch is on for a brief duration, the current flow in the auxiliary circuit remains minimal and does not induce substantial losses in the converter. The circuit diodes are all switched off under zero current switching and do not have the problem of reverse recovery. The suggested converter has been fully analyzed and a 150W prototype implemented to prove the theoretical analysis of the circuit

articleTitle: Analyzing the Effects of Intermittent Renewable Energy Participation in Wholesale Electricity Markets
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: With the continued global rise in investments in renewable energy technologies, the share of these resources in electricity generation has significantly increased. While these technologies provide numerous benefits, such as reducing CO2 emissions, decreasing reliance on fossil fuels, and creating new jobs, there are growing concerns about their direct and indirect negative impacts on electricity markets. If policymakers aim to provide significant quantities of power from intermittent renewable resources, it might significantly affect the market, as these resources may not consistently meet demand due to their reliance on natural conditions. Therefore, the growing integration of renewable energy sources (RES) in a restructured electricity market has created challenges, which are explored in this paper. The findings indicate that the integration of RES can lead to significant changes in market price behavior. A substantial share of RES in electricity generation capacity results in lower wholesale market prices, higher price spikes, and increased price volatility. Furthermore, an increased share of renewable energy sources may diminish the effectiveness of forward contracts in curbing market power within wholesale electricity markets. Also, the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind can increase the cost of ancillary services due to the greater need for storage and emergency supply.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Cogging Torque in Coaxial Magnetic Gear by Rotors Skew-Shaping
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The torque between an input and an output shaft can be transferred by magnetic gears without the need for physical contact. In certain instances, the design specifications of the entire system dictate that magnetic gears have an integer gear ratio. This leads to a higher cogging torque in the high-speed rotor (internal rotor), which results in vibration and acoustic noise. Creating an uneven air gap and skewing one of the three coaxial magnetic gear rotors are common ways to lower cogging torque. In this paper, in order to significantly reduce the cogging torque with an integer gear ratio, a coaxial magnetic gear with a skewed modulator is proposed. In addition, the proposed structure uses an internal rotor with a non-circular surface to create an unequal air gap. The proposed structure is optimized by a genetic optimization algorithm and Maxwell finite element software to simultaneously minimize the cogging torque and maximize the torque density. The results of comparing the proposed structure with the conventional spoke-type structure show a reduction of 88.3% and 5% in terms of the cogging torque and core losses, respectively.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Optimization and Strategic Evaluation of Sustainable Energy Options for Powering Large User Demand
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Power networks are critical for operators to improve productivity and permit the increased integration of renewable energy sources (RES). Nonetheless, swings in demand and nonlinear restrictions exacerbate renewable energy sources' intermittent and unpredictable nature. This research proposes combining wind farms with battery energy storage technologies to minimize production and carbon emissions costs in conventional power plants. This upgrade takes into account the costs associated with traditional fossil fuel-dependent units as well as carbon emissions. The simulation includes five conventional producing sources and large user load consumers. The results show that the improved problem formulation considerably increases the ability and effectiveness of optimizing power plant production schedules.

articleTitle: Real-Time Pricing for Electric Vehicle Charging Stations Using Deep Reinforcement Learning Under Congestion and Peak Shifting
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The extraordinary penetration of electrical vehicles (EV), and the need of energy management considering these movable load, lead charging network operator (CNO) to preparing comprehensive pricing algorithm. Unlike the previous studies in dynamic pricing which focused on single function optimization such as revenue improvement or network parameters, this study focuses on finding intelligent algorithm which can handles three major problems in charging station including congestion and peak shifting, and charging Time. The article proposes a new real time pricing (RTP) method which is data-based that derived of historical data. For this purpose, we implied a soft actor-critic (SAC) network in reinforcement learning (RL) equipped by deep neural network. The 99.98 percent of accuracy, shows a highly accurate performance of this study in real-time pricing.

articleTitle: Optimization of Wind-Battery Hybrid System Scheduling Simultaneously with a Demand Response Program: An Examination of Commercial Load
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Power systems are crucial for operators to optimize their performance and support the growing penetration of renewable energy sources (RES). However, RES are intermittent and variable, with load variations and nonlinear limitations exacerbated by these obstacles. This research presents a method for enhancing the management of optimum generation and carbon emissions costs of conventional power plants by combining wind farms with battery energy storage. This improvement considers the costs incurred by traditional units relying on fossil fuels and the expenditures related to carbon emissions. The simulation includes Commercial load customers and five traditional generating sources, and the results show that the ability and performance of power plant generation schedule optimization have significantly improved with the new issue formulation.

articleTitle: Single Switch High Voltage Gain DC-DC Converter with Low Voltage Stress for Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel high step-up converter with low semiconductors voltage stress. It combines a quasi-Z-source structure and voltage multiplier cells along with a passive clamp circuit to achieve a very high voltage gain required for renewable energy applications. In this converter, switch and most of the diodes operate at zero current switching (ZCS) condition. Therefore, the switch turn-on switching loss along with the diodes reverse recovery problem are alleviated. This converter does not need a high turns ratio for the coupled inductors to achieve a high voltage gain and thus, needs a smaller magnetic core. The passive clamp circuit successfully absorbs leakage inductance energy. Common input-output grounding and a low-ripple input current are attained in the proposed converter. The converter theoretical analysis, comparison with recently introduced converter counterparts, and simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Single-Input Dual-Output Quadratic DC-DC Topology with Ultra-High Voltage Gain for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This study introduces an ultra-high-voltage gain (VG) DC-DC topology with dual output ports, featuring a quadratic-based structure tailored for renewable energy applications. The proposed design incorporates a coupled inductor (CI) combined with a quadratic boost stage to achieve substantial voltage elevation. Voltage gain is adjustable through two main standards: the duty cycle of the switches and the turn ratio of the dual-winding CI, enhancing design flexibility. Notable characteristics of this converter include its high VG, reduced voltage stress (VS) on switching elements,, common ground (CG) connection amid ports, and synchronized operation of switch. The merits of this configuration are underscored by comparative analysis with similar topologies. The converter's effectiveness is demonstrated through tests on a 440W prototype operating at a 50 kHz switching frequency, with a 20V input and equal output voltages of 240V.

articleTitle: Super Twisting Control Strategy Implemented on a Bidirectional DISO DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this paper, a fast dynamic and chattering-free control strategy called super-twisting controller (STC) is introduced. The STC controller generates a proper input signal to the bidirectional dual input single output (BDISO) DC-DC converter by means of pulse width modulation (PWM) technique. There are several ports in this BDISO converter, including, a DC power source port, an energy storage port, and an output port. The particular consideration about the design of the STC controller is to force the controlled states to seek their desired values with the fastest dynamic possible along with the lowest over/undershoot in various modes, including buck, boost, and bidirectional mode. Through simulation outputs, the effectiveness of the introduced control methodology is evaluated, and its performance is compared to that of a conventionally well-tuned proportional-integral (PI) and a fixed-frequency sliding mode (FSMC) controller by means of MATLAB/SIMULINK software.

Author Keywords: Bidirectional Dual Input Single Output Converters (BDISO)

articleTitle: Cooperative Energy Scheduling of Renewable-based Multi-microgrid Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper proposes a cooperative energy management for smart distribution systems consisting of microgrids. The proposed model utilizes a centralized approach to manage the daily scheduling of microgrids in order to minimize their total costs. Microgrids integrate the battery energy storage system to control the probabilistic behavior of renewable generation. Also, real-time price-based demand response programs are considered to best model the flexibility of microgrids. The microgrids form a big alliance to reduce the complexity of the optimization problem and reduce the total cost of microgrids. Compared to the decentralized model, the proposed model reduces operation cost and unsupplied energy by 5.46 % and 100 %, respectively.

articleTitle: A New Equal/Unequal Multilevel Inverter Structure Based on Developed H-Bridge
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel structure of equal and unequal multi-level inverters with low electrical equipment. The proposed multi-level inverter Includes an H-bridge, on the sides of which the level generation cells are placed. These cells consist of 6 unidirectional power switches along with 5 DC sources. The proposed multi-level inverter has two advantages over classical and recent multi-level inverters, including the production of higher levels compared to the number of components and the use of low-power devices (low stress of electrical devices). In this paper, a comprehensive comparative study between multilevel inverter topologies has been done to validate the proposed inverter. The result of the comparative analysis shows that the proposed inverter is significantly superior to other inverters. The results related to the loss simulation of the proposed inverter are presented. The achievement of the proposed inverter and the nearest level modulation is confirmed by the simulation results.

articleTitle: A High Efficiency and Compact Small EV Charger
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Modern industries require efficient charging solutions for portable and mobile systems. This paper presents a novel grid-connected portable charger powered by isolated current transformers, designed to draw energy directly from power lines. By clamping onto these lines, the charger induces AC, which is then regulated to provide optimal voltage for battery charging. The proposed design features an interleaved resonant converter structure, achieving high efficiency and broad compatibility with varying input voltages. This configuration enables a variable DC-bus voltage, allowing the resonant converter to operate near its resonant frequency for maximum performance. To ensure a lightweight and efficient design, the converter eliminates traditional transformers, relying instead on a capacitor in the resonant structure for isolation. The charger supports many applications, offering compatibility with 1–6 cell Li-Ion batteries. Simulations for output voltages from 4.2 to 50 V and power levels from 5 to 500 W demonstrated a peak efficiency of 94%, validating the effectiveness of the proposed solution for grid-connected charging applications.

articleTitle: Optimization of Wind Power System with Fuzzy-PI Control for Axial Flux-Switching PM Generator
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This study investigates a wind power generation system featuring an axial field flux-switching permanent magnet generator with a twisted structure (AFFSPM-TS), combined with direct-drive control. The system employs a fuzzy-PI method for voltage reference control, providing advantages such as simple structure, high power efficiency, and reliability compared to other systems. A wind power generation system is implemented using DSP. The experiments focus on the optimization of tip speed control strategy to maximize wind power output under various wind speed conditions. Fuzzy-PI controllers are used for voltage reference management, improving the system's response to environmental changes and enhancing overall performance. Experimental results confirm the performance and reliability of the introduced control strategy. for managing active and reactive power, demonstrating the system's robustness and precision across various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Modular DAB Converter Power Balancing with Variable Inductor
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter is one of the suitable isolated structures for high-power applications. With the increasing demand for energy, consumers such as electric vehicles and similar devices require significant electrical power. Due to the limitations of power handling in switching converter components, such as the maximum current and voltage ratings of semiconductors, it has become necessary to connect multiple converters in a modular configuration to achieve the required total power. However, this approach can result in power imbalance among the modules due to non-idealities and mismatched component characteristics in each module. In this paper, by modifying the inductor of the DAB converter, power balance between the modules is achieved. Finally, two DAB converter modules providing a total power of 10 kW are simulated and verified in MATLAB software.

articleTitle: Dual-Stage Soft-Switched High Gain Three-Port Converter for Integrated Hybrid PV-Battery Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper introduces a high-gain, soft-switching non-isolated three-port converter (TPC) designed for renewable energy systems interfacing photovoltaic (PV) sources, battery storage, and loads. The topology integrates two boost converter stages with a shared DC link and a reconfigurable battery port, enabling flexible power transfer pathways. A uxiliary resonant circuits provide zero current switching (ZCS) and zero voltage switching (ZVS), significantly reducing s witching losses and enhancing efficiency. T he control strategy employs Incremental Conductance MPPT for optimizing PV output and independent PI control for maintaining stable load voltage, with dynamic mode selection based on real-time PV, battery, and load conditions. The proposed converter achieves high voltage conversion ratios, stepping up low PV voltages efficiently, and demonstrates high performance (91–98% efficiency) with a voltage gain of 12 at 2 kW, as validated through simulations.

articleTitle: Integrated Wind Energy and Battery Energy Storage Systems as a Sustainable Solution for Industrial Loads
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Power networks are essential for operators to enhance productivity and facilitate the increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RES). Nonetheless, fluctuations in demand and nonlinear constraints intensify renewable energy sources' intermittent and unpredictable characteristics. This paper presents a way for merging wind farms with battery energy storage systems to optimize the management of output and carbon emissions costs in conventional power plants. This enhancement considers the expenses associated with traditional fossil fuel-dependent units and the expenditures related to carbon emissions. The simulation has five conventional generating sources and industrial load consumers. The findings indicate that the enhanced issue formulation significantly improves the ability and efficacy of optimizing power plant production schedules.

articleTitle: A Simple Pre-Estimation Method for Calculating the Inductance of a Variable Inductor
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a simple method for predicting inductance in applications of variable inductors with ferrite cores. Today, switching converters are widely used for voltage and current level conversion in renewable energy applications. The variation of inductance in switching converters improves the voltage gain range and other converter characteristics. In this paper, through the analysis of core saturation, a simple circuit model is proposed to predict inductance when the core reaches saturation. This model enables designers to predict inductance variations prior to the winding of the core and the construction of the inductor. Two approaches regarding core permeability are analyzed: the well-known Brauer relationship and a proposed alternative. Finally, the proposed method has been validated and tested on two types of cores, includes E42 and E55.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Mitigation of Direct Torque Control of IM Based on a Novel 5-Level Torque Hysteresis Band Controller Suitable for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Recently, Direct Torque Control (DTC) is considered a remarkable solution for achieving appropriate torque control behavior in AC motors. Nevertheless, it still suffers from disadvantages such as the large torque and current ripples. An altered direct torque control (MDTC) for induction motors is illustrated based on an innovative switching procedure using a 5-level torque hysteresis band controller. In the presented method, along with the existing voltage vectors in the conventional direct torque control (CDTC), several intermediate-voltage vectors are applied to increase the flexibility of the drive system against different torque variations. The presented method mitigates torque and speed ripples and improves the flux regulation at low speeds. Finally, the simulation results obtained from MATLAB/SIMULINK confirm the effectiveness of the proposed drive system.

articleTitle: A Transformerless Step-Up Converter with Lossless Snubber
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This study presents a high voltage gain converter featuring a lossless snubber, designed to achieve high efficiency and reliability. Key attributes of the proposed converter include zero current switching (ZCS) during switch turn-on, zero voltage switching (ZVS) during switch turn-off, minimal use of additional circuit switches, and a low number of snubber elements. The design effectively absorbs leakage inductance energy, eliminates reverse recovery problem in diodes, and ensures increased voltage gain with reduced voltage stress on the switch. Additional advantages include PWM control and low circulating current in the auxiliary circuit, making it a robust and efficient solution for high voltage gain applications. To validate the circuit analysis, a 150W prototype was implemented.

articleTitle: Identification of Effective Factors on Formation Generator Coherent Groups for Islanding Detection for Renewable Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Identification of coherent groups and determining the frequency of their oscillations in power system is very important. The coherent groups that are created in the power system and their behavior in the isolation of power system are necessary. In this paper, a number of factors such as error position, Power system structure, constant inertia of generators and operating point of power system in each section are investigated and generator coherent groups are separated. The results show that this factors are affected on the coherent groups. In this paper, for determining the coherent groups, rotor oscillation of the generators is used, which this is a common method for the grouping of generators. These simulations are carried on the network of 9 generators designed at Digsilent environment.

articleTitle: An Optimal Conservative Voltage Reduction Strategy in Active Distribution Networks Using Coordinated Operation of RES, OLTC, ESS, and SCB
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Voltage control has become a significant challenge with the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources (RESs) in active distribution networks (ADNs). Variations in the output power of wind and photovoltaic (PV) units can lead to voltage drops or voltage rises in different buses of the network. Also, there are continuous variations in the load demand of the network. These issues necessiate appropriate coordination of voltage-control equipment to prepare optimal operation for ADN. Regarding voltage-dependency of load demands, this paper proposes an optimal conservative voltage reduction (CVR) strategy to improve efficiency and scheduling of ADNs. This strategy is designed with the coordinated operation of on-load tap-changer (OLTC), energy storage systems (ESS), switchable capacitor banks (SCBs), and RESs. The problem is modeled as a mixed non-linear programming (MINLP) and implemented in the GAMS environment. The efficiency of the proposed method is evaluated by applying it on the IEEE 33-bus system in different cases where the results show improved network performance and operating parameters.

articleTitle: Using Phase-Change Materials in Distribution Network Transformers for Thermal Loss Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this project, we will examine the feasibility of using PCMs to reduce the temperature of oil distribution transformers. First, we will provide a review of PCM usage in equipment and their application. Then, we will investigate the nature of these materials. Next, a sample PCM of Paraffin type along with nano-magnesium hydroxide is used to analyze the thermal behavior of a 400kVA oil transformer in MATLAB. The thermal curve of the transformer under the worst conditions is obtained using its thermal model. We prove that adding the studied PCM to the transformer reduces the temperature of the oil and the transformer body at high temperatures within a simulation. Given that the studied PCM releases its thermal energy gradually at temperatures lower than the breakdown limit, it reduces the transformer temperature gradually, which in turn increases the transformer's efficiency and lifespan.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Renewable Energy Production Through Solar-Biogas Hybrid System as an Alternative to Fossil Fuels (Case Study: Kermanshah)
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This study explores the feasibility of integrating biogas from municipal waste with solar energy in a hybrid power plant at Kermanshah University of Technology. Located near a municipal waste disposal site, the power plant combines photovoltaic panels and a natural gas turbine generator. The research investigates substituting natural gas with biogas to address energy security challenges and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Detailed analysis of waste input data and biogas production potential reveals that this integration can enhance energy efficiency, promote sustainable waste management, and reduce reliance on fossil fuels. The findings highlight the benefit to support renewable energy adoption and optimize local resources for a more sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Dynamic Reconfiguration of Network Structure and Connected Microgrids for Resilience Enhancement Under Storm Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of destructive storms pose a significant challenge to power systems, potentially leading to transmission line failures and reduced network resilience. Optimizing network topology can mitigate the negative impacts and enhance operational efficiency under critical conditions. This study aims to improve the resilience of distribution networks against storms by identifying vulnerable lines and optimizing the network configuration. Monte Carlo simulation is employed to assess the failure probability of critical lines within the network. Subsequently, the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is applied to determine the optimal network configuration, considering three types of switches: connecting microgrids to the main grid, interconnecting microgrids, and reconfiguring the main distribution network. The load demand, wind speed, solar radiation, and ambient temperature are modeled probabilistically using normal and Weibull distributions to reflect realistic operating conditions. The results indicate that the outage of four critical lines significantly reduces network reliability. However, by reconfiguring the network, system losses are reduced by up to 25%, and the load-carrying capacity is increased by 30%. Moreover, maintaining load supply in islanded operation mode significantly contributes to system resilience. The proposed strategy can serve as an effective solution for disaster management and improving the operational reliability of distribution networks during severe storms. The findings of this study are generalizable to other distribution networks and can contribute to enhancing the resilience of power systems against natural disasters.

articleTitle: Tuning Variable Speed Wind Turbine Controller Using a Data-Driven Approach: The TD3 Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controller and its variants are widely employed in industrial systems due to their well-documented benefits. This paper investigates the implementation of reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms for tuning controller parameters in the pitch control of a variable-speed wind turbine operating in the full-load region. Due to the complex dynamical behavior of wind turbines, tuning the controller has significant challenges. The proposed method is model-free and conducts controller tuning solely based on system's data. The Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients (TD3) algorithm, an off-policy Actor-Critic method, is employed for tuning the parameters as it does not necessitate a system model. The efficacy of the TD3- based tuning method is demonstrated through simulations on 4.8 MW variable speed variable pitch wind turbine, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Stochastic Framework for Smart Home Energy Management: Integrating Demand Response and Renewable Resources Using Improved ABC Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a home energy management system that optimizes the electricity demand of home appliances according to demand response programs. This home is equipped with renewable energy, including wind turbines and solar panels. The uncertainty of renewable energy is modeled using stochastic programming. Different types of loads have been used in this home, and the mentioned loads have been properly adjusted and distributed to minimize the cost of energy and deal with fluctuations in renewable energy. An improved Artificial Bee Colony algorithm has been used to solve this problem. The results confirm that the introduced model can efficiently harvest all possible energy of the wind-solar system, manage uncertainty, minimize cost, and operate independently of the grid. These goals are achieved through the complex coordination of load management strategies in the proposed load response framework, which leads to an efficient and flexible energy management system. The numerical results reported in this paper show the effectiveness of the proposed method. The proposed plan is generally usable and valuable for any other type of smart home.

articleTitle: A Review of Microgrid and Virtual Power Plant Strategies for Effective DERs Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Various perspectives, methodologies, constraints, and goals contribute to the scheduling challenge of distributed energy resources (DERs) in power systems. This issue can be addressed through different frameworks. Among the well-known concepts that address this issue within their respective frameworks are microgrids and virtual power plants (VPPs). These approaches all hold unique significance and can be used for a variety of purposes. As a result, it is important to evaluate and analyze existing literature and research in this area. The paper examines DER scheduling problems from a variety of perspectives, including modeling techniques, solution methods, reliability, emissions, uncertainty, stability, demand response (DR), reactive power generation, and multiobjective scheduling in the context of microgrids and VPPs. Researchers can use this review to identify potential microgrid and VPP scheduling applications from diverse perspectives.

articleTitle: Holistic Centrality: A New Approach to Evaluate Dynamics of Complex Power Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach, termed “Holistic Electrical Centrality”, to evaluate the dynamics of complex power networks by extending traditional operational betweenness centrality to encompass all system buses involved in active and reactive power flows. Unlike existing operational and structural centrality measures, which often overlook critical buses such as generation points, the proposed holistic approach treats generators and demands as separate pendant nodes, ensuring a comprehensive analysis of power flow dynamics. Through simulations on the IEEE 14-Bus test system, we demonstrate that holistic betweenness measures effectively assign non-zero values to previously overlooked buses and exhibit stronger correlations with system states, i.e., voltage phase and magnitude, compared to traditional measures. The results highlight the potential of holistic centrality to enhance grid management strategies, including resource allocation, vulnerability assessment, and reliability improvement.

articleTitle: AI and IoT in Energy Conservation: Challenges, Opportunities, and Trends
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The rapid advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) have paved the way for innovative solutions to address global energy challenges. This paper explores the integration of AI and IoT in energy conservation, focusing on their combined potential to optimize energy consumption, enhance system efficiency, and support sustainable development. AI-driven predictive analytics and machine learning algorithms enable accurate energy demand forecasting and real-time decision-making, while IoT devices facilitate seamless data collection, monitoring, and control of energy systems. The synergy of these technologies has been instrumental in transforming energy management across various sectors, including smart grids, industrial automation, and smart buildings. However, their adoption comes with significant challenges, such as data security, interoperability, and the high cost of deployment. This review discusses the current state of AI and IoT in energy conservation, identifies key challenges, highlights emerging opportunities, and examines future trends, such as the role of blockchain and edge computing in decentralized energy systems. The paper concludes by emphasizing the need for interdisciplinary research and collaboration to unlock the full potential of AI and IoT in creating sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Stochastic Energy Management in Multi-Microgrid Systems Considering Energy Efficiency Improvement Strategies: A Multi-Objective Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources into power systems has led to the development of multi-microgrid systems to play a pivotal role in energy systems. These systems are made of integrated microgrids which can operate autonomously to tackle issues of grid flexibility thus making the grid more flexible. Supply and demand of energy are unpredictable due to the volatile weather conditions, consumption rates as well as changes in the market price, hence the need for a stochastic analysis schedule. This paper examines the stochastic energy scheduling method used in multi-microgrid systems through a comprehensive analysis. The primary contributions include (1) a two-stage stochastic programming framework for multi-microgrid energy management considering the independence index, and ENS simultaneously (2) an innovative method of oxygen extraction during hydrogen conversion to boost energy efficiency and reduce costs; and (3) A taxonomic analysis of superior Pareto solutions which applies the paired comparison matrix alongside the Technique for Order of Priority by Similarity to an Ideal Solution conducts a detailed category assessment. The numerical analysis demonstrates that the implementation of a P2H system alongside the proposed method with multi-energy systems results in a daily cost savings of 763∃.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wind Power Forecasting Through a Hybrid Deep Learning Approach: Long Short-Term Memory Integrated with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Accurate prediction of wind energy generation plays a vital role in integrating renewable energy sources efficiently into electrical grids. This study explores the use of advanced artificial intelligence methods for forecasting wind power production at two meteorological stations located in Khomein and Saveh, Iran. A new hybrid model is proposed, combining LSTM networks with an attention mechanism. This approach surpasses traditional methods like Random Forest and XGBoost by better capturing intricate temporal dynamics and adjusting to fluctuating wind conditions. The results demonstrate the model's potential to improve grid stability and optimize energy management.

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Hub Performance Using the Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO) Algorithm for Integrated Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Energy hubs are essential infrastructures for integrated energy management, optimizing consumption and distribution while enhancing system stability and efficiency. This study presents a deterministic model aimed at minimizing the operating costs of energy grids, where energy hubs coordinate distributed generation and storage systems. To address uncertainties in load, energy prices, renewable energy production, and mobile storage consumption, an adaptive robust optimization approach is employed. The nonlinear and non-convex problem is solved using the Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO) algorithm, which achieves superior results compared to other methods, with an objective function value of 4253.7, a convergence iteration of 1130, and a computational time of 313.043 seconds. These outcomes underscore the effectiveness of IPSO in optimizing integrated energy systems.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of a Robot for Power Transmission Insulator Cleaning
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: One of the key factors contributing to electrical failures and disruptions in transmission lines is the accumulation of dust and pollution on the surface of electrical insulators. Regular cleaning of electrical insulators is essential to remove contamination and prevent damage to transmission lines. Laser technology has emerged as an innovative method for cleaning surfaces contaminated by environmental pollutants. In this paper, a quadrotor equipped with four motors is investigated as a platform for delivering a laser cleaning system to insulators. The quadrotor is modeled to enable more realistic control simulations. The modeling and control of the quadrotor are critical components of our system's design. The dynamic simulation of the quadrotor is performed using ADAMS software, and after the dynamic analysis of the robot, the control system is designed and simulated using MATLAB. Finally, a maneuver is simulated to test the performance of the quadrotor's control system and evaluate the efficiency of the dynamic model.

articleTitle: A Bidirectional Three-Phase on-Board Integrated EV Charger Employing Dual-Inverter Drive
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: To overcome the key challenges in the widespread adoption of electric vehicles, this article introduces a bidirectional three-phase integrated on-board battery charger designed for electric vehicles with a three-phase open-ended winding machine. The vehicle's motor is powered by a dual inverter consisting of two three-phase traction inverters. These inverters employ two interleaved switching patterns to significantly reduce current ripple throughout the charger. The charger functions as a three-phase power factor correction converter. In this approach, the motor windings are utilized as DC inductors for the battery charger, effectively preventing torque generation while charging. The article provides a detailed explanation and analysis of the proposed integrated charger. Moreover, a fast and simple control strategy is introduced to reach near unity power factor. The feasibility and performance of the system are verified through simulations, confirming the theoretical deductions. The proposed charger achieves over 97% peak efficiency while complying with grid current harmonic standards.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis and Optimal Sizing of Distributed Generation Resources to Improve Network Reliability and Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Enhancing the performance and reliability of power distribution networks under critical conditions is one of the fundamental challenges in power system planning. This study presents a comprehensive approach for the capacity determination of distributed generation (DG) units. In the first phase, sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulation with 1000 iterations were employed to identify the critical lines that have the most significant impact on network performance based on key performance indicators, including Expected Energy Not Supplied (EENS), Voltage Deviation (VD), Power Losses (PLOSS), and Load Ability (LAL). Subsequently, the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm was utilized to optimize the DG capacity to minimize power losses, voltage deviation, expected energy not supplied, and operational costs. The distributed generation units, after sensitivity analysis and identification of critical lines, were placed near these lines to reduce their sensitivity. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach can effectively reduce power losses by 70%, voltage deviation by 25%, and expected energy not supplied by 40%, ultimately improving the network's reliability. This approach provides a practical and effective framework for the optimal design and operation of power distribution networks under critical conditions.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of DC-to-AC Ratio on Power Generation and Optimal Scenario Selection for Grid-Connected Solar Farms: A Case Study in Iran
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: With the growing global emphasis on expanding solar power capacity, employing optimized designs to minimize the construction costs of solar power plants is essential. A critical parameter in photovoltaic system design is the selection of an appropriate DC-to-AC ratio during the planning phase. This ratio significantly impacts the construction costs of a solar power plant. This study examines the energy output of a 6.25 MW solar farm utilizing bifacial solar panels across a range of DC-to-AC ratios from 1 to 1.2. Simulations for each scenario are conducted using PVSyst software. Key factors analyzed include the bifacial coefficient, temperature variations, economic optimization, clipping losses, panel degradation, mismatch losses and soiling losses, and seasonal variations, all aimed at determining the optimal number of inverters. The results indicate that reducing the DC-to-AC ratio, and thereby increasing the number of inverters, does not necessarily yield higher energy output over a 25-year operational period. Conversely, increasing the DC-to-AC ratio reduces the required number of inverters, leading to lower construction costs for the solar power plant.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Stability of Electric Vehicle Charging Station Under Parameter Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper investigates the small-signal stability of standalone Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCSs). The mathematical model of an EVCS is derived, enabling detailed analysis of system behavior under dynamic conditions. Eigenvalue analysis reveals the influence of key factors such as power load, LC filters, and line parameters on system stability. Notably, it is observed that poorly damped LC filters can significantly reduce system damping, introducing high-frequency oscillations that compromise operational reliability. Conventional stability assessment methods, including modal analysis, often overlook the impact of parameter uncertainties-such as variations in converter dynamics and network configurations-potentially leading to inaccurate results. To address these challenges, a frequency-dependent virtual impedance approach is introduced. This method effectively reshapes the high-frequency impedance of DC bus voltage control units, enhancing damping performance and mitigating oscillatory behavior. By incorporating parameter uncertainties into the stability framework, this work provides a robust methodology for ensuring reliable operation of standalone EVCSs in dynamic and uncertain parameters, contributing to the advancement of resilient and efficient energy systems.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Robust Operation of Power-Gas Integrated System with Penetration of Wind Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The fast development of wind energy installation in power systems accompanied by the interdependency of power and gas systems due to the application of gas-fueled power generating units (GPGUs) and electric-driven gas system compressors (EGSCs) intensified the importance of coordinated operation of power and gas integrated systems (PGISs) with penetration of wind energy. In this paper, a two-stage robust framework is presented for optimal operation of the PGIS under intermittency of wind energy and demand uncertainties, in which the first stage provides day-ahead scheduling of the PGIS, while the second stage addresses the real-time operation. To enable tractable computation, the Column and Constraint Generation (C&CG) algorithm is used to offer an efficient way of solving the proposed model. Numerical simulations on a 24bus-20node PGIS demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Integrating Renewable Energy Systems: A Review of Economic Strategies and Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In recent years, growing environmental concerns and increasing energy demand have highlighted the importance of renewable energy sources as a sustainable and economically viable solution. One of the fundamental challenges in this field is the optimization of economic costs associated with the production, distribution, and consumption of renewable energy. This review paper examines various optimization methods for the efficient management of renewable energy-based systems. In this context, objective functions related to cost, efficiency, and energy sustainability are analyzed. Also, the methodology and techniques for solving optimization problems, including various algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and others, are explored. Additionally, recent studies on the integration of renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, hydrogen, and biomass, and their impact on reducing economic costs, are reviewed.

articleTitle: Coordinated Design of FACTS and RES to Improve Synchronization Process During the Power System Restoration
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In the process of power system restoration, desirable islands are first formed, and after the initial loading on each island and the relative stability of each, the islands are connected to each other through synchronization operations. In this situation, the most significant challenge for network operation experts will be minimizing the standing phase angle between the two endpoints of the two subsystems. The most common measures for this challenge include continuously increasing or decreasing the network load, continuously increasing or decreasing the network generation, and in some cases, reconfiguring the network. Another solution is the use of FACTS devices to control the steady-state phase angle smoothly and quickly. These devices can reduce the steady-state phase angle difference between two subsystems more effectively and rapidly by applying precise and fast control signals. Alongside the mentioned solutions, utilizing renewable resources for smooth changes in the generation sector is also considered a suitable tool for improving the synchronization process of the islands. Therefore, this paper introduces an optimal and coordinated design between FACTS devices and renewable resources to enhance the synchronization of subsystems with the aim of minimizing the steady-state phase angle between two adjacent islands and reducing the dynamic fluctuations of the power system. The selected decision variables in this proposed scheme include the location of FACTS devices, their control parameters, load values at each bus, and the optimal use of renewable resource capacity. Since the proposed optimization process involves a large number of variables, the system under study is complex and nonlinear, and the objective functions are also nonlinear, the proposed optimization problem is modeled as a single-objective nonlinear problem, and heuristic algorithms are used to solve it. The proposed heuristic technique for executing the optimization process of the mentioned problem is a learning-based optimization algorithm. To evaluate the proposed method, the problem has been applied to the IEEE 39-bus power system. Simulation results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed method in reducing the steady-state phase angle and accelerating synchronization operations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Overcurrent Relay Performance in Power Systems with Distributed Generation: An AI-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The effectiveness of overcurrent relays is essential for managing faults in power systems. As the integration of distributed generation sources increases within the power grid, the likelihood of errors in fault detection also rises. In certain situations, distributed generation can diminish fault currents, leading to delays in relay operation. This delay can damage existing equipment as faults persist in the network. Additionally, distributed generation may cause relays to malfunction, disconnecting healthy feeders instead of the ones experiencing faults. To address these challenges, this paper presents the development and modeling of an artificial intelligence algorithm designed to facilitate the integration of distributed generation into the power system without modifying the existing overcurrent relays. The algorithm also identifies optimal locations for distributed generation sources within the network. The modeling was conducted using MATLAB, and the implementation and validation of the model were performed with DigiSilent software.

articleTitle: Coati-Based Optimal Design of a 2-DOF PID Controller for a KY Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Renewable energy is increasingly being recognized as a viable solution to the world’ growing energy demands.
