DC-DC converters, however, can be utilized to address low output voltage of renewable sources requirements. Nonlinearity is one of the main problems with DC-DC converters. This characteristic results in voltage instability, causing nonlinear variations in response to circuit parameter changes. Consequently, the accurate selection of the controller and the proper design of its components are essential. In this paper, a two-degree-of-freedom PID (2-DOFPID) controller is designed using the Coati Optimization Algorithm (COA) for KY buck-boost converter. In order to ensure that the output voltage remains steady regardless of disturbances, the coefficients of the mentioned controller have been optimized using the COA. For minimizing the time-domain indexes of the closed-loop system, the suggested controller coefficients are obtained using the ISTSE index as the objective function. The performance of the 2-DOFPID controller and conventional PID controller was compared using various evaluation indexes under different cases to assess the proposed controller's performance and closed-loop system behavior.

articleTitle: Optimized Explainable Tabular Transformer Model for Fault Localization in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Detecting and locating faults in DC microgrids (DCMGs) is essential for maintaining their reliability and stability. This research introduces an optimized tabular transformer (TabNet) model to accurately locate the fault due to its ability to selectively focus on important features and provide interpretable results, making it well-suited for analyzing the complex relationships in fault-induced traveling wave (TW) signals. To improve the model's performance, TabNet hyperparameters were fine-tuned through grid search. In this work, key input features were extracted from TWs generated during fault events as input to TabNet. These features include the magnitude, polarity, and time of arrival of TWs, which were obtained using a refined time-frequency analysis of high-order synchrosqueezing transform. To make the model's predictions easy to understand, local interpretable model-agnostic explanations were used to explain how different features influenced the results. The proposed method was tested on a simulated DCMG under different fault scenarios. Its performance was compared with other existing techniques. The results showed that the method is more accurate and reliable in locating faults.

articleTitle: Comparison of Rigid and Modular Oscillating Wave Surge Converters
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Climate change and the increasing demand for clean energy have led to a growing interest in marine renewable energy, particularly wave energy converters (WECs). This study compares two distinct geometrical designs of bottom-hinged, nearshore oscillating wave surge converters (OWSCs): Rigid and Modular. OWSCs are also known as Flap-type wave energy converters. An OWSC is usually installed perpendicular to the wavefront and converts the surge motion of the wave into rotational motion through a hinge and captures wave power. Simulations were carried out with the boundary element method using the three-dimensional radiation/diffraction theory, which is employed by the ANSYS-AQWA software. Regular Airy wave under different wave periods from 5 to 15 s and constant wave height (2 m) was considered as an environmental condition based on wave records of Chabahar port. At first, a validation procedure has been done. Then, the study determines the optimal damping coefficient for the power take-off (PTO) system in relation to the average absorbed power. Based on the results, at optimum condition, the Modular OWSC is 260 percent better than the Rigid type.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on Market and Energy Trading Mechanism in MV-EHs
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: With an emphasis on their importance in con temporary power systems, this study examines the electricity trading as well as trading processes in Multi vectored Energy Hubs (MV-EHs). Multiple-source-integrated MV-EHs are essen tial to decentralised energy procurement as well as management. The first section of this study compares centralized as well as decentralization methods for introducing numerous markets clearing processes that are used within power hubs to maintain equilibrium demand alongside supply. After that, it explores several energies trading systems, emphasizing how MV-EHs relate to them. These systems include bilateral arrangements, peer-to-peer trading, as well as virtual power plants (VPPs). Furthermore, a variety of procedures are explored that facilitate efficient dealings, which include as procedures for optimization, auction-based strategies and neural network approaches. This study's last section addresses the opportunities and challenges for the development of MV-EH trade in electricity, with a focus on impending technological integration along with regulatory adap tation. Through this analysis, readers will gain a comprehensive understanding of how evolving technologies and market factors will impact the trading of electricity in MV-EHs in years to come.

articleTitle: Lithium Battery SOH Estimation: A Novel Octave and LSTM Hybrid Neural Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The lithium battery (LIB) has emerged as a prominent area of research in energy and industrial applications, due to its superior energy density and efficient energy delivery capabilities. This study addresses the critical requirement for accurate State of Health (SOH) estimation as a significant challenge. The primary objective of this study is to utilize key battery health characteristic parameters to improve the accuracy and computational speed of SOH. Significant gaps have been identified in recent methodologies, particularly in terms of SOH estimation accuracy, computational speed, and simulation parameters. To address these limitations, a novel hybrid neural network (NN) approach is proposed, integrating octave convolution (OCT) and long short-term memory (LSTM). To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in the optimization process, a comparative analysis is conducted against Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), OCT, LSTM, and CNN-LSTM architectures. The results indicate a significant reduction in the mean squared error (MSE), decreasing from 80.21 percent in CNN to 0.0758 percent in the proposed OCT-LSTM model. Furthermore, the root mean square error (RMSE) exhibits a substantial reduction of 64.91 percent and 58.14 percent compared to the LSTM and CNN-LSTM models, respectively. The simulation parameters used in this study were reduced from 41,228 for the CNN-LSTM model to 38,668 for the OCT-LSTM model. Empirical results show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in the number of parameters, MSE, RMSE, and estimation accuracy. These findings highlight the method's enhanced efficiency, computational speed, and precision, emphasizing its potential as a significant advancement in this domain.

articleTitle: Management of Renewable Energy Resources and Demand Response in Electricity Retailers with the Presence of Water Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Electric vehicles and hydrogen storage systems, including electrolyzers, hydrogen tanks, and fuel cells, provide significant flexibility for energy management in the smart grid. This paper presents a solution for electricity selling price determination and energy management for a retailer in the smart grid under uncertainty conditions. In this work, several sources of energy supplies are considered: the shared market, bilateral contracts, distributed generation units, renewable energy sources - photovoltaic systems and wind turbines -, plug-in electric vehicles, and hydrogen storage systems. A neural network is used in order to predict uncertainty conditions concerning the shared market price, consumer demand, temperature, solar radiation, and wind speed. The retailer will determine and compare the electricity selling price under three scenarios: fixed tariff, time-of-use tariff, and real-time tariff in the smart grid. Additionally, it is assumed that the system operator prefers to use groundwater resources, but environmental issues such as drought, dust storms, landslides, and wetland degradation hinder this exploitation. To maximize retailer profits and reduce groundwater usage, a multi-objective optimization is proposed. The proposed model is formulated as a mixed-integer programming problem and solved using GAMS software. The results of three types of electricity selling price determinations, considering the demand response program, have been analyzed and compared. According to the results, the retailer's profit increased by 12%, 12.8%, and 10.2% in the mentioned tariffs, respectively.

articleTitle: Advanced Voltage and Reactive Power Control in Modern Distribution Networks with High Penetration of Distributed Generation: A Fuzzy Logic-Based Approach for 2025 Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 12th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energies and Distributed Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel, efficient, and computationally lightweight approach for voltage and reactive power control in distribution networks with high penetration of distributed generation (DG) using advanced Fuzzy Logic techniques. Unlike traditional methods that rely on complex and time-consuming calculations, the proposed methodology ensures simplicity while maintaining precision and scalability. The core innovation lies in the dynamic modeling of DG's active and reactive power equations, which are adapted to the unique characteristics of electrical distribution networks, including overhead line conductors. This ensures optimal integration of DG without causing voltage violations or instability at the point of interconnection. To validate the accuracy and practical applicability of the proposed approach, extensive simulations were conducted on the IEEE 34-Node Test Feeder using ETAP software. The study evaluates the impact of capacitive compensation structures and DG integration under various load scenarios across three distinct cases, offering a comprehensive analysis of system performance. Results demonstrate significant improvements in voltage stability, reactive power management, and overall system efficiency. Additionally, the proposed framework provides a robust decision-making tool for optimal DG utilization, addressing the emerging challenges of modern power distribution systems in 2025 and beyond. This work sets a new benchmark for sustainable and intelligent voltage control in future smart grids.
